sections.overview: The Scalloped Ribbonfish is a rarely encountered ribbon-shaped fish recorded in tropical and temperate oceans worldwide.
sections.identification: Adults have a slender ribbon-like body, reddish dorsal fin and black tail; juveniles are silvery with dark blotches and a scalloped belly edge.
sections.habitat: It is an open-water fish; adults have been reported swimming vertically, head uppermost.
sections.diet: Reported foods for ribbonfishes include fishes, squid and crustaceans.
sections.behavior: Young fish shelter under jellyfish, while adults are oceanic.
sections.reproduction: It is oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae.
sections.ecology: It belongs to Trachipteridae, a family of ribbonfishes in which the jaws can protrude markedly during feeding.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global Least Concern assessment from 2013.
